_about: Clarity tests sent to OpenJev by the reply and question clarity hooks. Read by scripts/governance/clarity_jev.py. All tests of a hook go in ONE request: the eval showed tests answer worse when sent alone, so limits hold only for this exact set. A test blocks when its value is past block_at in the direction bad_when; null means log only. Limits come from clarity_eval.py on state/clarity/labelled.jsonl (eval-2026-11-23.md). Change a test's wording or the ORDER of tests only with a re-run: order shifts scores by up to 1 point.
framing: Below is a message from an AI coding assistant to its owner, a busy product manager who is not an engineer. The owner reads it cold, between meetings. They did not see the assistant's work, files, plans, code, agents or earlier messages, and they do not know any of the assistant's internal names, codes, step numbers or ticket ids unless the message explains them.

plain_language.instructions: How much of the text a smart 18-year-old with no technical background could understand.

unknown_terms_list.instructions: Picture the owner reading this once. How many separate times would they stop and think 'what is that?' because of a name, code, id, file, step number or made-up term the text does not explain in plain words?

unknown_terms_count.instructions: Count the distinct words, names, codes or ids in the text that the owner would have to ask about before understanding it. Ignore anything the text explains in plain words.

self_referential.instructions: The text explains things mainly by naming other internal labels, documents or earlier steps, instead of describing the product, the users or the outcomes the reader already knows.

process_not_results.instructions: The text mostly describes the assistant's own process (tools it ran, ids, line numbers, internal steps) instead of the results and what they mean for the reader.

zero_context_clarity.instructions: How easily a smart reader who saw none of the work can follow the text on the first read.
criteria: Cannot follow it without asking what things mean
Follows parts of it, but key parts need explaining
Follows most of it, with one or two unclear terms
Follows all of it on the first read

can_decide_from_text.instructions: The owner could choose an option from this text alone, because each option says in plain words what will happen and what it costs or risks.
